# nish/term-probe

What the terminal a program runs in can do (its colours, keyboard protocol, graphics and size), asked of it once at start and read from its answer.

```ts
import {
  TERM_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS,
  TermCaps,
  TermEnv,
  TermProbe,
  probeQueries,
} from "nish/term-probe";
```

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="probeQueries" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#probequeries">

Every query the probe asks, as one write; `TermProbe` reads the answers.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="TermCaps" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#termcaps">

What a terminal can do, from its answers to `probeQueries` and the environment.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="TermEnv" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#termenv">

The environment the probe reads, each variable "" when unset.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="TermProbe" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#termprobe">

A probe in progress: made when `probeQueries` is written, at `sentAtMs`, for a window of `cols` by `rows` cells, fed what the terminal sends.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

<scalar-callout type="info">

A program writes `probeQueries(env)` in one write, then feeds what the
terminal sends back to a `TermProbe` until `done()` (the terminal answered
the last query) or `timedOut(now)`, and reads the `TermCaps` from `result()`.
The module is pure: the environment comes in as a `TermEnv`, times are the
caller's milliseconds as `f64` from any origin, and nothing here reads,
writes or waits.

</scalar-callout>

```ts
import { TermEnv, TermProbe, probeQueries } from "nish/term-probe";

const env: TermEnv = new TermEnv();
env.term = "xterm-256color";
const probe: TermProbe = new TermProbe(env, 80, 24, 0.0);
const queries: string = probeQueries(env); // write these to the terminal
// …feed each read: probe.feed(bytes, count, nowMs), until probe.done() or probe.timedOut(nowMs)
console.log(`${probe.result().colors}`);
```

- `TermEnv` — the environment variables the probe reads, each "" when
  unset, one field each in camelCase: `term` (`TERM`), `colorterm`
  (`COLORTERM`), `termProgram` (`TERM_PROGRAM`), `tmux` (`TMUX`), `sty`
  (`STY`), `sshConnection`, `sshClient` and `sshTty` (`SSH_CONNECTION`,
  `SSH_CLIENT`, `SSH_TTY`), `noColor` (`NO_COLOR`), `nishTermGraphics`
  (`NISH_TERM_GRAPHICS`) and `nishTermFps` (`NISH_TERM_FPS`, which the probe
  carries for the renderer and does not read).
- `probeQueries(env)` — every query, in this order, as one string:
  XTVERSION `CSI > q`, DECRQM for synchronized output `CSI ? 2026 $ p` and
  pixel mouse `CSI ? 1016 $ p`, kitty's keyboard flags `CSI ? u`, a kitty
  graphics query `APC G i=31,s=1,v=1,a=q,t=d,f=24;AAAA ST`, XTSMGRAPHICS
  for the sixel colour registers `CSI ? 1 ; 1 ; 0 S`, the cell size
  `CSI 16 t`, the text area size `CSI 14 t`, a true-colour background set
  and read back with DECRQSS (`CSI 48 ; 2 ; 1 ; 2 ; 3 m`, `DCS $ q m ST`,
  `CSI m`), and DA1 `CSI c` last. Terminals answer in order, so the answer
  to DA1, which every terminal gives, means the rest are in. Under tmux
  (`TMUX` set) the queries only the outer terminal can answer — kitty
  graphics and the two sizes — go inside tmux's passthrough,
  `DCS tmux; … ST` with each ESC doubled; under GNU screen (`STY` set) the
  sizes go inside screen's `DCS … ST`, and the kitty graphics query and
  DECRQSS, which hold an ST of their own and which screen would forward
  rather than answer, are left out. On the Linux console (`TERM=linux`)
  both are left out too: it has no string states and would print them. DA1 is never wrapped: the multiplexer
  answers it, so a multiplexer that forwards no reply still ends the probe.
- `TermProbe` — the probe in progress, made when the queries are sent.
  `feed(bytes, count, nowMs)` decodes a read through its own `KeyDecoder`
  (`nish/term`), keeping the replies and holding back every other event (a
  key typed while the probe ran) for `heldEvents()`, in order. `done()` is
  true once DA1 is answered; `timedOut(nowMs)` once `timeoutMs` (250 by
  default) has passed since the send with no answer to DA1. Either way
  the program then calls `finish(nowMs)` once: it gives up whatever the
  decoder still holds (a key cut off at the end of the read with DA1, say)
  and returns `heldEvents()` complete, and later reads go to the program's
  own decoder. `rttMs()` is the time from the
  send to the answer to DA1, -1 before it. `result()` reads the replies and
  the environment into a `TermCaps`, and can be called at any point.
- `TermCaps` — what the terminal can do: `colors` (16, 256 or 16777216),
  `trueColor`, `sync`, `kittyKeyboard`, `kittyGraphics`, `sixel`,
  `sixelRegisters`, `cellWidthPx` and `cellHeightPx`, `pixelMouse`,
  `multiplexer` ("none", "tmux" or "screen"), `linuxConsole`, `remoteHint`,
  `answered`, `probeRttMs`, `graphics` ("kitty", "sixel", "halfblock" or
  "ascii"), `name` and `overrides`; each field's comment says where it
  comes from.

The environment decides where the terminal cannot answer, and where the
user says so: `COLORTERM=truecolor` or `24bit` means true colour, as does
a DECRQSS that reads the 24-bit background back; otherwise a `TERM` with
`256color` in it means 256 colours, and anything else 16. `TERM=linux` is
the Linux console: 16 colours, ASCII graphics, no kitty keyboard and no
synchronized output, whatever it answered. `NO_COLOR` set to anything
(no-color.org) means 16 colours and touches nothing but colour.
`NISH_TERM_GRAPHICS` names a graphics backend to use instead of the one the
answers pick; a pixel backend the terminal did not answer for is refused
when it would come out as garbage or nothing — on the Linux console, under
a multiplexer, or when the terminal answered nothing at all. `overrides`
says what each variable did, refusals included. The match is exact:
`kitty`, `sixel`, `halfblock` or `ascii`, lower case, nothing around it.

Under a multiplexer the probe sees the multiplexer first. tmux and screen
answer DA1 themselves, so `done()` comes on their answer, before any reply
forwarded through the passthrough; `probeRttMs` is the round trip to the
multiplexer, and graphics come from what the multiplexer itself answers
(tmux's own sixel, say). The environment is taken at face value: an
`SSH_*` variable or `COLORTERM` left in a tmux session by the client that
started it still counts, though the client attached now may differ.

## TermCaps

What a terminal can do, from its answers to `probeQueries` and the environment.

```ts
class TermCaps
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new TermCaps()` | Caps of a terminal that answered nothing: 16 colours, ASCII. |
| `answered: boolean` | Whether the terminal answered DA1; false when the probe timed out. |
| `cellHeightPx: i32` | A cell's height in pixels: `CSI 16 t`, else the text area's from `CSI 14 t` over the rows; 0 unknown. |
| `cellWidthPx: i32` | A cell's width in pixels: `CSI 16 t`, else the text area's from `CSI 14 t` over the columns; 0 unknown. |
| `colors: i32` | How many colours to draw with: 16, 256 or 16777216. |
| `graphics: string` | The graphics backend to draw with, best first — "kitty", "sixel" (256 registers or more), "halfblock", "ascii" — after `NISH_TERM_GRAPHICS`. |
| `kittyGraphics: boolean` | Whether kitty graphics are there: the query answered `OK`. |
| `kittyKeyboard: boolean` | Whether the kitty keyboard protocol is there: `CSI ? flags u` answered. |
| `linuxConsole: boolean` | Whether this is the Linux console (`TERM=linux`). |
| `multiplexer: string` | The multiplexer in between: "none", "tmux" (`TMUX` set) or "screen" (`STY` set). |
| `name: string` | The terminal's name and version from XTVERSION, else `TERM_PROGRAM`, else "". |
| `overrides: string` | What the environment forced, one `VARIABLE: effect` per entry joined by `; `; "" when nothing. `nish/term-io` adds `NISH_TERM_FPS`'s, which the controller applies. |
| `pixelMouse: boolean` | Whether SGR mouse reports in pixels (mode 1016) are known: DECRPM answered set or reset. |
| `probeRttMs: f64` | The time from the send to the answer to DA1, in milliseconds; -1 unanswered. |
| `remoteHint: boolean` | Whether the session looks remote (`SSH_CONNECTION`, `SSH_CLIENT` or `SSH_TTY` set), so slow. |
| `sixel: boolean` | Whether sixel is there: DA1 lists 4. |
| `sixelRegisters: i32` | How many sixel colour registers there are, from XTSMGRAPHICS; 0 unanswered. |
| `sync: boolean` | Whether synchronized output (mode 2026) is known: DECRPM answered set or reset. |
| `trueColor: boolean` | Whether 24-bit colour works: `COLORTERM`, or the background DECRQSS read back. |

## TermEnv

The environment the probe reads, each variable "" when unset.

```ts
class TermEnv
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new TermEnv()` | An environment with every variable unset. |
| `colorterm: string` | `COLORTERM`: `truecolor` or `24bit` where the terminal has 24-bit colour. |
| `nishTermFps: string` | `NISH_TERM_FPS`: a frame rate for the renderer; carried, not read, by the probe. |
| `nishTermGraphics: string` | `NISH_TERM_GRAPHICS`: a graphics backend to use instead of the probed one, `kitty`, `sixel`, `halfblock` or `ascii`. |
| `noColor: string` | `NO_COLOR`: set to anything to ask for no colour (no-color.org). |
| `sshClient: string` | `SSH_CLIENT`: set by sshd for a remote session. |
| `sshConnection: string` | `SSH_CONNECTION`: set by sshd for a remote session. |
| `sshTty: string` | `SSH_TTY`: set by sshd for a remote session with a terminal. |
| `sty: string` | `STY`: set inside GNU screen. |
| `term: string` | `TERM`: the terminal type, such as `xterm-256color` or `linux`. |
| `termProgram: string` | `TERM_PROGRAM`: the terminal's name where it sets one, such as `iTerm.app` or `Apple_Terminal`. |
| `tmux: string` | `TMUX`: set inside tmux. |

## TermProbe

A probe in progress: made when `probeQueries` is written, at `sentAtMs`,
for a window of `cols` by `rows` cells, fed what the terminal sends.

```ts
class TermProbe
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new TermProbe(env: TermEnv, cols: i32, rows: i32, sentAtMs: f64)` | A probe whose queries were written at `sentAtMs` to a window of `cols` by `rows` cells. |
| `answeredAtMs: f64` | When DA1 was answered; -1 before. |
| `cols: i32` | The window's width in cells, to turn `CSI 14 t` into a cell width. |
| `decoder: KeyDecoder` | The decoder the terminal's bytes go through. |
| `env: TermEnv` | The environment the queries were made for. |
| `held: TermEvent[]` | Every other event so far, in order: what the user typed during the probe. |
| `replies: TermEvent[]` | The replies so far, in order. |
| `rows: i32` | The window's height in cells, to turn `CSI 14 t` into a cell height. |
| `sentAtMs: f64` | When the queries were written. |
| `timeoutMs: f64` | How long to wait for the answer to DA1 (`TERM_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS` by default). |
| `done(): boolean` | Whether DA1 has been answered, so every reply is in. |
| `feed(bytes: u8[], count: i32, nowMs: f64): void` | Decode `bytes[0, count)`, read at `nowMs`. |
| `finish(nowMs: f64): TermEvent[]` | End the probe at `nowMs`: what the decoder still holds — an ESC or the start of a key that came in the read with DA1, or an unfinished reply on a timeout — is given up (the ESC as a key, the reply as nothing) and `heldEvents` returned complete. Call it once, when `done()` or `timedOut` ends the probe, and hand every later read to the program's own decoder. |
| `heldEvents(): TermEvent[]` | The events that were not replies — keys typed, a paste — in the order they came, for the program to handle. |
| `result(): TermCaps` | What the terminal can do, from the replies so far and the environment. |
| `rttMs(): f64` | The time from the send to the answer to DA1, in milliseconds; -1 before it. |
| `take(events: TermEvent[], nowMs: f64): void` | Take in `events`: replies kept, DA1 marking the probe done, the rest held. |
| `timedOut(nowMs: f64): boolean` | Whether `timeoutMs` has passed since the send with DA1 unanswered. Once it has, it calls `finish(nowMs)`, so `heldEvents` is complete. |
